claim: C. elegans forms a memory of particular foods after experience and displays behavioral plasticity by increasing the feeding response when they subsequently recognize the familiar food.
source_text: Here, we show that the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans forms a memory of particular foods after experience and displays behavioral plasticity, increasing the feeding response when they subsequently recognize the familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1-3 showing differential feeding rates on familiar vs novel bacteria.

claim: Recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons.
source_text: We found that recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons, which subsequently increase serotonin release.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by calcium imaging data in Figure 12 showing ADF activation in response to familiar bacteria.

claim: ADF neurons increase serotonin release in response to familiar food.
source_text: We found that recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons, which subsequently increase serotonin release.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 11 showing increased serotonin-positive cells after exposure to familiar food.

claim: Released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally.
source_text: The released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally and directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments showing ADF (extrapharyngeal) serotonin affects MC neurons, and NSM (pharyngeal) serotonin does not affect feeding on familiar food.

claim: Serotonin directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ.
source_text: The released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally and directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments in Figure 8 showing SER-7 expression in MC neurons restores feeding response.

claim: Worms sense the taste and/or smell of novel bacteria, which overrides the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding by suppressing the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
source_text: Our data suggest that worms sense the taste and/or smell of novel bacteria, which overrides the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding by suppressing the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by conditioned media experiments in Figure 14 and calcium imaging showing ADF is only active on familiar bacteria.

claim: Familiarity discrimination has a significant impact on the pattern of food intake across species.
source_text: Familiarity discrimination has a significant impact on the pattern of food intake across species.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement supported by citations to prior literature on feeding behavior across species.

claim: Recognition is the ability to identify and to judge a recently encountered item as having been presented previously.
source_text: Recognition is the ability to identify and to judge a recently encountered item as having been presented previously (Brown and Aggleton, 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition from established literature, supported by citation to Brown and Aggleton, 2001.

claim: Recognition is classified into two types: recollection and familiarity discrimination.
source_text: Recognition is classified into two types: recollection and familiarity discrimination.
evidence_reasoning: This classification is from established neuroscience literature, as indicated by the citation to Brown and Aggleton, 2001.

claim: Recollection is knowledge of prior occurrence with vivid contextual details.
source_text: Recollection is knowledge of prior occurrence with vivid contextual details.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition from established literature in the context of recognition memory.

claim: Familiarity discrimination is mere sensation of prior occurrence and thus does not accompany episodic memory.
source_text: In contrast, familiarity discrimination is mere sensation of prior occurrence and thus does not accompany episodic memory (Brown and Aggleton, 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition from established literature, supported by citation.

claim: Mere exposure to particular food alters subsequent consumption of the food in many different species.
source_text: Accumulated studies show that mere exposure to particular food alters subsequent consumption of the food in many different species (Pliner et al., 1993; Wang and Provenza, 1996; Diaz-Cenzano and Chotro, 2010; Morin-Audebrand et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies across different species.

claim: Feeding regulation by familiarity discrimination is conserved across species.
source_text: Accumulated studies show that mere exposure to particular food alters subsequent consumption of the food in many different species (Pliner et al., 1993; Wang and Provenza, 1996; Diaz-Cenzano and Chotro, 2010; Morin-Audebrand et al., 2012), suggesting that feeding regulation by familiarity discrimination is conserved across species.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from multiple cited studies showing similar patterns across species.

claim: Some species including humans consume familiar food more actively than novel food.
source_text: Some species including humans consume familiar food more actively than novel food (Diaz-Cenzano and Chotro, 2010), probably to avoid possible pathogens.
evidence_reasoning: The consumption pattern is supported by citation; the reason (avoiding pathogens) is speculative.

claim: Other species consume familiar food less actively than novel food, probably to assure balanced nutrition intake.
source_text: In contrast, other species consume familiar food less actively than novel food (Wang and Provenza, 1996), probably to assure balanced nutrition intake.
evidence_reasoning: The consumption pattern is supported by citation; the reason (balanced nutrition) is speculative.

claim: C. elegans is an attractive model system for study of feeding regulation due to its genetic tractability and simple anatomy.
source_text: Its genetic tractability and simple anatomy make the bacteria-eating roundworm C. elegans (Schafer, 2005) an attractive model system for study of the process.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about C. elegans as a model organism, supported by citation.

claim: The nervous system in C. elegans senses various aspects of food, such as the efficiency with which it supports growth and its pathogenicity, and triggers behavioral plasticity.
source_text: The nervous system in C. elegans senses various aspects of food, such as the efficiency with which it supports growth (Shtonda and Avery, 2006) and its pathogenicity (Zhang et al., 2005), and triggers behavioral plasticity.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citations to prior studies on C. elegans food sensing.

claim: The nervous system in C. elegans can form memories of various olfactory or gustatory cues.
source_text: The nervous system can also form memories of various olfactory or gustatory cues (Bargmann, 2006), which is likely to be crucial for the recognition of familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior work on C. elegans learning and memory.

claim: C. elegans discriminates familiar food from novel food and selectively increases feeding in response to familiar food.
source_text: Here, we show that C. elegans discriminates familiar food from novel food and selectively increases feeding in response to familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 1-3.

claim: The memory of familiar food in C. elegans lasts for at least 7 hours.
source_text: The memory of familiar food lasts for at least 7 hr.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figures 1D,E and 2B-E showing maintained feeding preference after 7-8 hour interval.

claim: Wild-type worms feed more actively on familiar food than novel food after a 7- to 8-hr interval from training.
source_text: Wild-type worms feed more actively on familiar food than novel food.
evidence_reasoning: Directly supported by feeding rate measurements in Figures 1, 2, and 7.

claim: The neurotransmitter serotonin increases feeding in C. elegans.
source_text: Recognition of familiar food increases the feeding response by activating serotonin signaling via SER-7
evidence_reasoning: This is implicit in the section heading and supported by data showing serotonin treatment increases feeding rates (Figure 4C-D).

claim: Familiarity of food does not alter the feeding rates in tph-1(mg280) mutants.
source_text: Familiarity of food does not alter the feeding rates in tph-1(mg280).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figures 4A-B and Figure 5 showing no difference between familiar and novel food in tph-1 mutants.

claim: Exogenous serotonin treatment selectively increases feeding rates of wild type worms on novel food to the level of the worms on familiar food.
source_text: Exogenous serotonin treatment selectively increases feeding rates of wild type worms on novel food to the level of the worms on familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figure 4C-D showing serotonin treatment eliminates the difference between familiar and novel food.

claim: ser-7(tm1325) is defective in increasing feeding response to familiar food compared to novel food.
source_text: ser-7(tm1325) is defective in increasing feeding response to familiar food compared to novel food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figures 4E-F and 7A-D showing reduced differential response in ser-7 mutants.

claim: Serotonin controls feeding positively via SER-7 and negatively via SER-4 and MOD-1.
source_text: Serotonin controls feeding positively via SER-7 and negatively via SER-4 and MOD-1.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic analysis of receptor mutants in Figures 4G, 6, and 7.

claim: The feeding rate of the ser-4; mod-1; ser-7 triple null mutant is not altered by serotonin treatment.
source_text: The feeding rate of the ser-4; mod-1; ser-7 triple null mutant is not altered by serotonin treatment.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figure 4G showing no response to serotonin in triple mutant.

claim: Serotonin signaling via SER-7 that activates the feeding response is more active on familiar food than novel food.
source_text: Serotonin signaling via SER-7 that activates the feeding response is more active on familiar food than novel food.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from comparison of wild-type and ser-7 mutant feeding rates under different conditions, shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Among five serotonin receptor null mutants, only ser-7(tm1325) failed to activate feeding in response to serotonin.
source_text: Among five serotonin receptor null mutants, only ser-7(tm1325) failed to activate feeding in response to serotonin.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figure 6 testing multiple serotonin receptor mutants.

claim: A null mutation in ser-4 decreased the feeding rate in presence of serotonin but the effect was relatively small.
source_text: A null mutation in ser-4 also decreased the feeding rate in presence of serotonin but the effect was relatively small.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing modest effect of ser-4 mutation.

claim: Serotonin is detected in five types of neurons in C. elegans: NSM, ADF, HSN, AIM, and RIH.
source_text: Serotonin is detected in five types of neurons in
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about C. elegans neuroanatomy, though the sentence is incomplete in the manuscript.

claim: tph-1 expression in ADF, but not in NSM, restores feeding rate in the tph-1 null mutant.
source_text: tph-1 expression in ADF, but not in NSM, restores feeding rate in the tph-1 null mutant.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments in Figure 8A-B.

claim: The rescue effect of ADF tph-1 expression is suppressed by loss of ser-7, but not by loss of mod-5.
source_text: The rescue effect is suppressed by loss of ser-7, but not by loss of mod-5.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic interaction experiments in Figure 8A.

claim: ADF-minus animals feed significantly less in response to familiar food.
source_text: ADF-minus animals, but not NSM-minus animals, feed significantly less in response to familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by laser ablation experiments in Figure 8C-D.

claim: NSM-minus animals do not show reduced feeding in response to familiar food.
source_text: ADF-minus animals, but not NSM-minus animals, feed significantly less in response to familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by laser ablation experiments in Figure 8C-D.

claim: Expression of ser-7 cDNA driven by the flp-2 promoter or by the flp-21 promoter fully restored the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to serotonin.
source_text: Expression of ser-7 cDNA driven either by the flp-2 promoter or by the flp-21 promoter (MC, M4, and other neurons) but not by the ser-7b promoter (M4 only) fully restored the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to serotonin.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments in Figure 8E.

claim: Expression of ser-7 cDNA in M4 only (driven by ser-7b promoter) did not restore the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to serotonin.
source_text: Expression of ser-7 cDNA driven either by the flp-2 promoter or by the flp-21 promoter (MC, M4, and other neurons) but not by the ser-7b promoter (M4 only) fully restored the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to serotonin.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments in Figure 8E.

claim: The rescue effect of pflp-21::ser-7 was suppressed by blocking cholinergic transmission from MC to the pharyngeal muscles.
source_text: The rescue effect was suppressed by blocking cholinergic transmission from MC to the pharyngeal muscles.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experiments using eat-2 mutation in Figure 8E.

claim: Expression of ser-7 cDNA driven by the flp-2 promoter or by the flp-21 promoter fully restored the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to familiar food.
source_text: Expression of ser-7 cDNA driven either by the flp-2 promoter or by the flp-21 promoter fully restored the feeding rate in the ser-7 null mutant in response to familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic rescue experiments in Figure 8F.

claim: SER-7 in MC activates pharyngeal pumping.
source_text: both pflp-21::SER-7 and pflp-2::SER-7 fully rescued the feeding rate in the ser-7 mutant in response to familiar food as well as serotonin...suggesting that SER-7 in MC activates pharyngeal pumping.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from rescue experiments showing overlapping expression in MC is sufficient for rescue.

claim: Serotonin released from extrapharyngeal ADF increased feeding in response to familiar bacteria mainly by activating SER-7 in MC directly, which in turn activates cholinergic transmission from MC to the pharyngeal muscles.
source_text: In summary, we conclude that serotonin released from extrapharyngeal ADF increased feeding in response to familiar bacteria mainly by activating SER-7 in MC directly, which in turn activates cholinergic transmission from MC to the pharyngeal muscles.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis conclusion based on multiple lines of experimental evidence from genetic, ablation, and rescue experiments.

claim: ADF is more active on familiar bacteria than novel bacteria.
source_text: We tested the hypothesis first by asking if ADF is more active on familiar bacteria than novel bacteria by directly measuring the response of the ADF neurons to novel and familiar bacteria using ratiometric calcium imaging.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by calcium imaging data in Figure 12 showing differential ADF responses.

claim: ADF releases more serotonin in response to familiar bacteria than novel bacteria.
source_text: We then asked if ADF releases more serotonin in response to familiar bacteria than novel bacteria.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from immunohistochemistry data in Figure 11 showing increased serotonin uptake in other neurons when animals are on familiar food.

claim: In C. elegans, serotonin is taken up by serotonergic neurons AIM, RIH, and NSM via the serotonin reuptake transporter MOD-5.
source_text: Since direct measurement of serotonin release from ADF in response to food is challenging, we developed a method to detect released serotonin indirectly by its uptake into other serotonergic neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about C. elegans serotonin system, implied by the experimental design.

claim: The increase in the number of serotonin positive serotonin-uptaking cells during the 1 hr incubation on familiar food was greater than the increase on novel food.
source_text: Consistent with our hypothesis, the increase in the number of serotonin positive serotonin-uptaking cells during the 1 hr incubation on familiar food was greater than the increase on novel food
evidence_reasoning: Supported by immunohistochemistry quantification in Figure 11D.

claim: Only familiar bacteria activate ADFs, which increases serotonin release from the neurons and subsequently activates the feeding response.
source_text: In conclusion, only familiar bacteria activate ADFs, which increases serotonin release from the neurons and subsequently activates the feeding response.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis conclusion based on calcium imaging and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Conditioned media from novel bacteria override the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding.
source_text: Conditioned media from novel bacteria override the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figure 14 showing reduced feeding when conditioned media from novel bacteria is added to familiar bacteria.

claim: Worms recognize familiar bacteria by their taste or smell.
source_text: To get insight into the mechanism, we tested if worms recognize familiar bacteria by their taste or smell.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from conditioned media experiments in Figure 14 showing soluble cues affect feeding.

claim: Perception of the smell and/or the taste of novel bacteria suppresses feeding activation on novel food by inhibiting the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
source_text: Our results that conditioned media from novel bacteria override the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria and suppress the feeding response (Figure 14) and that ADF is active only on familiar bacteria (Figure 12) indicate that perception of the smell and/or the taste of novel bacteria suppresses feeding activation on novel food by inhibiting the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from combining conditioned media experiments and calcium imaging data.

claim: At least two neural pathways act antagonistically in controlling the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
source_text: Given that familiar food substantially increased ADF activity compared to the baseline (Figure 12A,B), at least two neural pathways should act antagonistically in controlling the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that ADF shows increased activity on familiar food compared to baseline.

claim: ADF or its upstream neurons are positively regulated by perception of food and negatively regulated by perception of olfactory and gustatory cues of novel bacteria.
source_text: The simplest model would be that ADF or its upstream neurons are positively regulated by perception of food and negatively regulated by perception of olfactory and gustatory cues of novel bacteria
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed model based on the experimental observations, representing a speculative interpretation.

claim: C. elegans remembers two bacterial types for at least 24 hours.
source_text: Preliminary data show that C. elegans remembers two bacterial types at least for 24 hr (data not shown)
evidence_reasoning: Mentioned as preliminary data, though not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Serotonin transmission from ADF is critical for the learned aversion to pathogenic bacteria.
source_text: Interestingly, serotonin transmission from ADF was also shown to be critical for the learned aversion to pathogenic bacteria (Zhang et al., 2005; Ha et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Prior exposure to particular bacteria selectively increases feeding in response to those bacteria.
source_text: We first showed that regulation of feeding by familiarity discrimination is conserved in C. elegans by showing that (1) Prior exposure to particular bacteria selectively increases feeding in response to those bacteria
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figures 1-3.

claim: The behavior of increased feeding on familiar bacteria depends on the duration of exposure, but not on the timing of exposure or nutritional status.
source_text: The behavior depends on the duration of exposure, but not on the timing of exposure (Figure 3) or nutritional status (Figure 1B–E)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: The C. elegans nervous system may have evolved to increase the probability of consuming wholesome food by using past food experiences.
source_text: We speculate that the C. elegans nervous system may have evolved this way to increase the probability of consuming wholesome food by using past food experiences as in higher vertebrates and humans.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as speculation about evolutionary function.

claim: Naïve worms are attracted to the smell of pathogenic bacteria but develop aversion to it after experience.
source_text: It was previously shown that naïve worms are attracted to the smell of pathogenic bacteria but develop aversion to it after experience (Zhang et al., 2005; Ha et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Pathogenic bacteria kill worms in 4 hours.
source_text: The pathogenic bacteria kill worms in 4 hr (Zhang et al., 2005)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior study.

claim: An endocrine serotonin signal from ADF, not a local serotonin signal from NSM, may have been employed for the feeding activation on familiar food to systemically control multiple behaviors and physiological adaptations.
source_text: An endocrine serotonin signal from ADF, not a local serotonin signal from NSM, may have been employed for the feeding activation on familiar food to systemically control multiple behaviors and physiological adaptations.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of why the endocrine pathway might be used.

claim: NSM is a prominent reservoir of serotonin in the pharynx.

claim: NSM is implicated in regulating the enhanced slowing response on food.
source_text: NSM is implicated in regulating the enhanced slowing response on food (Sawin et al., 2000)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior study.

claim: NSM releases little or no serotonin in response to familiar food, which is insufficient to activate MC neurons in the pharynx.
source_text: One plausible explanation is that NSM releases little or no serotonin, which is insufficient to activate MC neurons in the pharynx in response to familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed lack of NSM effect on feeding.

claim: Serotonin from NSM has only a small effect on the enhanced slowing response.
source_text: This explanation does not contradict previously reported NSM function in the enhanced slowing response (Sawin et al., 2000) because serotonin from NSM has only a small effect on the behavior (Sawin et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Novel bacteria dictate activation of ADF and the subsequent serotonin-dependent feeding response in the natural habitat where more than one bacterial type are likely to grow mixed together.
source_text: Our study predicts that novel bacteria dictate activation of ADF and the subsequent serotonin-dependent feeding response in the natural habitat where more than one bacterial type are likely to grow mixed together.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction based on the experimental findings, extending to natural conditions.

claim: MC is essential for normal fast feeding on bacteria.
source_text: Among the pharyngeal neurons, MC is particularly interesting because it is essential for normal fast feeding on bacteria (Avery and Horvitz, 1989)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior study.

claim: SER-7 was suggested to activate MC.
source_text: SER-7 was suggested to activate MC (Hobson et al., 2006; Song and Avery, 2012).

claim: The flp-21 and the flp-2 promoters drive expression in several neurons, and the expression patterns of the two promoters overlap only in MC and M4.
source_text: The flp-21 and the flp-2 promoters drive expression in several neurons, and the expression patterns of the two promoters overlap only in MC and M4 (Kim and Li, 2004).

source_text: eat-2 encodes a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit specifically localized in the pharyngeal muscles postsynaptic to MC (McKay et al., 2004).

source_text: Thus, an eat-2 null mutation selectively blocks cholinergic transmission from MC to the pharyngeal muscles.

claim: SER-7 is expressed mostly in pharyngeal neurons.
source_text: SER-7 is expressed mostly in pharyngeal neurons (Hobson et al., 2006)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior expression analysis.

claim: Pharyngeal neurons regulate the motions of pharyngeal muscles.
source_text: SER-7 is expressed mostly in pharyngeal neurons (Hobson et al., 2006), which regulate the motions of pharyngeal muscles (Avery and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior functional studies.

claim: SER-7 is active to some extent even in absence of its ligand, serotonin (constitutive activity).
source_text: The difference may be due to constitutive activity of SER-7; that is, SER-7 is active to some extent even in absence of its ligand, serotonin (Hobson et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to prior characterization of SER-7 properties.

claim: Like the positive SER-7-mediated signal, the inhibitory SER-4- and MOD-1-mediated serotonin signaling is more active on familiar food than novel food.
source_text: Like the positive SER-7-mediated signal, the inhibitory SER-4- and MOD-1-mediated serotonin signaling is more active on familiar food than novel food, but it decreases the feeding rate.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from comparison of ser-7 single mutant and ser-4; mod-1; ser-7 triple mutant data in Figure 7.

claim: Like wild type worms, ser-4(ok512); mod-1(ok103) show increased feeding response on familiar food compared to novel food.
source_text: Like wild type worms, ser-4(ok512); mod-1(ok103) show increased feeding response on familiar food compared to novel food.
